# Purpose

This document explains the single R script `R/portfolio_stats.R`, which
computes per-symbol descriptive statistics for a portfolio of daily stock
closing prices. The goal is to give a reviewer a clear picture of what the
script does, what it expects, and what it returns — without having to read the
source line by line.

## Inputs

The function `portfolio_stats()` takes one argument:

- `prices`: a data frame with two columns
  - `Symbol` (character) — the stock ticker
  - `Close` (numeric) — the daily closing price

```{r example-input}
prices <- data.frame(
  Symbol = rep(c("AAA", "BBB"), each = 3),
  Close  = c(100.1, 101.4, 99.8, 50.2, 49.7, 51.0)
)
prices
```

## How it works

The function groups the data by `Symbol` and summarises each group with
`dplyr::summarise()`:

```{r function-body, eval=FALSE}
portfolio_stats <- function(prices) {
  stopifnot(all(c("Symbol", "Close") %in% names(prices)))
  prices %>%
    group_by(Symbol) %>%
    summarise(
      n         = dplyr::n(),
      mean_px   = mean(Close, na.rm = TRUE),
      median_px = median(Close, na.rm = TRUE),
      sd_px     = sd(Close, na.rm = TRUE),
      min_px    = min(Close, na.rm = TRUE),
      max_px    = max(Close, na.rm = TRUE),
      .groups   = "drop"
    )
}
```

## Outputs

A tidy data frame with one row per symbol and the columns `n`, `mean_px`,
`median_px`, `sd_px`, `min_px`, and `max_px`.

```{r run, echo=FALSE}
source("R/portfolio_stats.R")
portfolio_stats(prices)
```

# Reproducibility

Run `install.packages("dplyr")`, then `source("R/portfolio_stats.R")` and call
`portfolio_stats()` on any data frame with `Symbol` and `Close` columns. Only
synthetic data is used in this document.
